title: Explosions damage the Kerch Bridge linking Crimea to Russia for a second time
body:
In the early hours of 17 July 2023 explosions hit the Kerch Bridge, which links southern Russia with the Crimean Peninsula, annexed by Russia from Ukraine in 2014. According to an Associated Press report carried by Georgia Public Broadcasting, at least two people died and another was injured. Local authorities said a teenage girl was orphaned when her parents' car was apparently hit. Witness video showed a section of the road partially collapsed, and a parallel railway track appeared undamaged.

Russian authorities called the incident a terrorist attack carried out by Ukrainian special forces using two sea drones. Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova accused Ukraine and said it had help from United States and British intelligence. Ukraine did not claim responsibility. A spokesperson for Ukraine's Southern Command suggested Russia might have staged the explosions to undermine the Black Sea grain export deal, which expired that day.

The bridge is a key supply line for Russian forces in southern Ukraine and a symbol of Moscow's control over Crimea. Vladimir Putin drove the first vehicle across when it opened in 2018. Ukraine considers the bridge a legitimate military target. The July attack was the second significant strike on the bridge since October 2022, when a truck bomb damaged two sections.
